one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent regressed from a broken general ELF parser to a hardcoded offset approach covering only .rodata and .data (omitting .text), producing locally consistent but grossly under-covered output that fails the 75% reference-address requirement.
t_err_evidence: Step 7 creates extract.js that explicitly skips .text ('.text' || '.init' || '.fini' are excluded) while only targeting .data and .rodata; this is the first decisive mistake — omitting .text, the dominant section, guarantees insufficient coverage regardless of subsequent refinements.
t_commit_evidence: Step 14 abandons any attempt to fix the general ELF parser (after the debug logs in step 13 expose total parsing failure) and commits to a hardcoded approach using fixed file offsets for .rodata and .data only; from this point the agent never revisits the parser or considers .text, locking in the under-coverage outcome.
t_surface_evidence: Step 10: running 'cat out.json' returns '{}' — an empty JSON object — the first observable signal that the extractor failed to produce any values.
trigger_explanation: The agent never investigated which sections the task specification requires to be covered. It arbitrarily decided .text should be excluded (labeling it a 'code section') without checking whether the evaluator references .text addresses. This omission of spec-driven section selection drove the coverage shortfall. A secondary contributing factor is a knowledge gap about ELF64 field offsets, which caused the initial general parser to produce garbage metadata.
forewarning_evidence: Step 10 produces '{}' — empty JSON — despite the script having run without error. This is a clear warning that the extraction is broken, yet the agent responds by adding debug logs rather than reconsidering the section coverage strategy.
fabrication_evidence: Step 14 hardcodes file offsets (rodataFileOffset=0x2000, dataFileOffset=0x3000) and sizes (0x10) observed from a specific a.out via objdump; step 17 declares 'values match perfectly!' by cross-checking only against that same objdump output rather than the actual evaluation reference, treating local consistency as correctness while missing .text and using signed reads.
